collection_summary:
Original `top_k` instance filling a gap-3 category (top_k: 1 reg + 3 staged → 4 staged after this instance). **Technology/Civil Engineering** subdomain — new Civil Engineering subdomain under the existing Technology family (cycle-2 audit HYGIENE H1 corrected cycle-1 invented 'Engineering' top-level family to align with domain_taxonomy.md Technology family). Natural human query: 'What are the longest bridges in the world by main span — both overall and within each major structural type — and which country built each?'

Multi-wiki source plan (22 URLs): 5 Wikipedia per-type 'List of longest X bridge spans' master articles supply the universe + ranking (one master list per structural type — Suspension, Cable-stayed, Arch, Cantilever, Continuous truss); 17 per-bridge Wikipedia articles supply per-row Main Span + Country + Year of Completion via lead/infobox sections.

Result: 17 rows × 5 columns (Bridge PK + Type categorical + Main Span numeric + Country categorical + Year of Completion numeric), single-key PK on Bridge, 0 duplicates. Distribution by type: Arch 4, Cable-stayed 4, Cantilever 4, Continuous truss 1, Suspension 4. Country distribution: China 9 (dominates the modern top-K rankings across Arch, Cable-stayed, and Suspension types — all 4 Arch entries + 3 of 4 Cable-stayed + 2 of 4 Suspension), Japan 3, plus singletons for USA, UK, Canada, Russia, Turkey. Main Span range: 400 m (Ikitsuki continuous truss) to 2023 m (1915 Çanakkale suspension). Year of Completion range: 1890 (Forth Bridge cantilever) to 2025 (Changtai cable-stayed + Nanjing Xianxin suspension) — 135 years of major-span engineering.

Universe rule: top-4 longest-main-span bridges per each of the four primary load-bearing structural types (Suspension, Cable-stayed, Arch, Cantilever), PLUS the single longest continuous truss bridge (Ikitsuki). This 4+1 asymmetric partition is the staged universe — a `source_defined` claim type, not `exhaustive` top-K-uniform-K. The asymmetry is curator-decided: the continuous truss type's top-4 floor (~325 m) falls well below the visible engineering threshold the other four types occupy (all 4th-place entries exceed 500 m), so including continuous truss types past #1 would dilute the universe with bridges that fall outside the foregrounded-engineering threshold.

Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal + painters + extinctions + deserts + tennis + music-genres + olympians + spacecraft lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Bridge using Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved (e.g., '1915 Çanakkale Bridge' keeps the date prefix because 'Çanakkale Bridge' alone is ambiguous; 'Sutong Yangtze River Bridge' keeps the river qualifier because there are multiple Sutong-named structures); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (per-type master + per-bridge), 22 URLs total; (c) explicit selection rule for the 4+1 partition asymmetry committed at Stage-1 (documented in decision_log + temporal_note + open_questions); (d) source_defined claim type honestly reflects the curator-decision partition rule; (e) Wikipedia common-form names with diacritics preserved per article title (Akashi Kaikyō macron; 1915 Çanakkale cedilla; Tian'e Longtan ASCII apostrophe).
source_coverage_notes:
Twenty-two Wikipedia source URLs combine. Five per-type 'List of longest X bridge spans' master articles define the universe + ranking (one master list per structural type, each maintaining a top-N ranking by main-span length); 17 per-bridge articles supply per-row attribute values via infobox / lead sections.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_longest_suspension_bridge_spans): universe + ranking for Suspension partition. Top-4 entries staged (post-cycle-2): 1915 Çanakkale (2023 m), Akashi Kaikyō (1991 m), Nanjing Xianxin Yangtze River Bridge (1760 m, opened 2025), Yangsigang (1700 m). Cycle-1 staged Xihoumen (1650 m, 2009) at the #4 slot; cycle-2 audit (factual BLOCKING) caught that Xihoumen has been displaced — current master list places Nanjing Xianxin at #3 and Xihoumen at ~#6. Article's current top-5 entry (Nansha Bridge East span, 1688 m, China, 2019) is NOT staged because of the 4-per-type rule; documented as proposed_supplements alternative.
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_longest_cable-stayed_bridge_spans): universe + ranking for Cable-stayed partition. Top-4 entries staged (post-cycle-2): Changtai Yangtze (1176 m, completed 2025), Russky (1104 m, 2012), Husutong Yangtze River Bridge (1092 m, 2020), Sutong Yangtze (1088 m, 2008). Cycle-1 staged Changtai year as 2024 + Stonecutters (1018 m, 2009) at #4; cycle-2 audit (factual BLOCKING) caught (a) Changtai opened 9 September 2025 per per-bridge article infobox, and (b) Stonecutters has been displaced to rank ~5 by Husutong (1092 m > Sutong 1088 m, so Husutong sits at #3 and Sutong at #4).
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_longest_arch_bridge_spans): universe + ranking for Arch partition. Top-4 entries staged: Tian'e Longtan (600 m), Pingnan Third (575 m), Chaotianmen (552 m), Lupu (550 m). Sydney Harbour Bridge (503 m, Australia, 1932) is the most-iconic Western arch bridge but sits at #5-6 in the modern master ranking; NOT staged in the strict top-4 rule; documented as proposed_supplements alternative.
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_longest_cantilever_bridge_spans): universe + ranking for Cantilever partition. Top-4 entries staged: Quebec (549 m, 1917), Forth (521 m, 1890), Minato (510 m, 1974), Commodore Barry (501 m, 1974). The Cantilever type rankings are unusually stable — all 4 staged entries are 50+ years old.
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_longest_continuous_truss_bridge_spans): universe + ranking for Continuous truss partition. Only the type-#1 Ikitsuki Bridge (400 m, 1991) is staged. The #2 entry (Astoria-Megler, 376 m, USA, 1966) is documented as proposed_supplements alternative but excluded under the 4+1 partition rule.

Per-bridge Wikipedia articles (per-row attribute grounding):

This refines the canonical-source rule committed at Stage-1 to: per-bridge article wins for Main Span value when the per-bridge article is more detailed than the master table (infobox + lead concur) and the master-table value is unsupported by per-bridge sourcing.
- source_urls[15] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaotianmen_Bridge): 552 m; China (Chongqing); 2009.

- source_urls[19] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minato_Bridge): 510 m; Japan (Osaka); 1974.
- source_urls[20] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodore_Barry_Bridge): 501 m; United States (New Jersey-Pennsylvania); 1974.
- source_urls[21] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ikitsuki_Bridge): 400 m; Japan; 1991.

Validation note: every (Bridge, Type, Main Span, Country, Year of Completion) tuple is grounded in (a) the per-type master list confirming the bridge's structural-type assignment and rank-within-type, and (b) the per-bridge Wikipedia article supplying Main Span (m), Country, Year of Completion via lead/infobox. Main Span values match between the two sources for 16 of the 17 staged rows; the exception is Pingnan Third Bridge (575 m per-bridge article vs 560 m master arch table) — cycle-2 audit HYGIENE H2 resolved by adopting the per-bridge article value 575 m per the cycle-2 refined canonical-source rule. Canonical-source rule (post-cycle-2): per-bridge article wins for Main Span value when the per-bridge article is more detailed than the master table (infobox + lead concur on a value the master table does not corroborate); master per-type list wins for ranking (rank-within-type); per-bridge article wins for Country + Year of Completion (the per-bridge article is the entity-canonical source). The rank-within-type rule survived cycle-2: cycle-2 BLOCKING B1+B2 displaced Xihoumen Bridge and Stonecutters Bridge from their cycle-1 staged positions because the current master per-type lists rank them below the top-4 floor (master list is canonical for ranking even when individual per-bridge articles preserve historical rank-context).

Universe-size sanity: 17 staged rows = top-4 longest-main-span per the four primary load-bearing structural types (Suspension, Cable-stayed, Arch, Cantilever) PLUS the single longest continuous truss bridge (Ikitsuki). This 4+1 asymmetric partition is the staged universe rule. Across all 5 types, the master lists each enumerate dozens to hundreds of bridges — the staged 17 are a top-K-per-type subset, not exhaustive.
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with three documented risks resolved at staging. R1: per-type partition is a curator-decided choice — Wikipedia organizes longest-bridge lists by structural type, and 'longest bridges overall' would be dominated entirely by suspension bridges (the 5 longest spans overall are all suspension); the partitioned top-K-per-type approach exercises hierarchical_decomposition (secondary category) and gives the LLM a richer task than a flat top-5-overall query. R2: continuous truss type has a much lower span-ceiling than the four primary types (Ikitsuki at 400 m vs others' 4th-place at 500+ m) — committed to the 4+1 asymmetric partition rule at Stage-1, documented as a deliberate scope-defined choice. R3: the Cable-stayed #1 Changtai Yangtze River Bridge was completed very recently (2024-2025 window per Wikipedia); temporal_sensitivity=medium reflects the active churn at the top of modern Chinese cable-stayed and arch lists.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed specifically addresses bridges (the seed file's engineering-related questions are about other infrastructure). Closest seed-in-shape is the longest-rivers and tallest-buildings seeds (both top-K-by-physical-dimension shape) — bridges are a same-shape entity class in a different domain family.
- Category: top_k (primary, per-type top-K-by-main-span). Secondary: hierarchical_decomposition (universe partitioned by structural type, then top-K within each partition — Type → top-K bridges).
- Source plan: 22 Wikipedia URLs (5 per-type master lists + 17 per-bridge articles). Master lists define universe + ranking; per-bridge articles supply per-row attribute values.
- Expected shape: 17 rows × 5 cols, single PK on Bridge.
- Domain: Technology/Civil Engineering — Civil Engineering is a new subdomain under the existing Technology top-level family (cycle-1 staged 'Engineering/Civil Engineering' but cycle-2 audit HYGIENE H1 caught this invents a top-level family not in domain_taxonomy.md; corrected to 'Technology/Civil Engineering' per audit recommendation, aligning with the Technology family's documented subdomain pattern in domain_taxonomy.md).
- Entity-class diversity (encouragement): bridges as physical infrastructure are a NEW entity class for the benchmark. Sibling 'physical-dimension top-K' instances exist for natural features (deserts by area, rivers by length) but no prior instance covers engineered structures.
- Risks/adaptation: per the three pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) row count 17 is within the standard 15-25 band; (b) 4+1 partition asymmetry needs to be honestly framed as `source_defined` rather than `exhaustive` top-K; (c) Changtai Yangtze River Bridge completion-year uncertainty (2024 vs 2025) flagged for audit-cycle-1 verification; (d) some staged Chinese bridges (Tian'e Longtan, Pingnan Third) are obscure outside civil-engineering specialist lists — their inclusion is a deliberate source-faithfulness choice over LLM-knowability, per PKDB-Bench design philosophy.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Universe rule: top-4 longest-main-span bridges per each of the four primary load-bearing structural types (Suspension, Cable-stayed, Arch, Cantilever) PLUS the single longest continuous truss bridge (Ikitsuki, 400 m). Total 17 rows. The 4+1 asymmetry reflects a curator-decision: continuous truss bridges past #1 fall below the visible engineering threshold (~500 m) the other four types occupy at their 4th-place entries, so including continuous truss types past #1 would dilute the universe with bridges that fall outside the foregrounded-engineering threshold. claim_type = `source_defined` honestly reflects this curator-bounded scope rule (NOT `exhaustive` which would imply top-K-uniform-K across all 5 types).
2) Strict source-faithfulness over LLM-knowability: at Stage-1 the option to substitute iconic bridges (Humber, Great Belt East, Sydney Harbour Bridge, New River Gorge) into the Suspension and Arch partitions was considered and rejected. The substituted version would replace the obscure Chinese mega-bridges (Yangsigang, Xihoumen, Tian'e Longtan, Pingnan Third) with iconic Western/Australian bridges that the LLM is more likely to know parametrically. Rejected because (i) PKDB-Bench's design philosophy is source-faithful universe definition (per curation_protocol.md and the consistent pattern across the 13 staged Ready instances); (ii) substituting iconic bridges would force claim_type to be `source_defined` with curator-judgment scope, making the universe rule fuzzy; (iii) modern Chinese mega-bridges are a real and growing share of the world's longest-span engineering — having them in the staged universe gives the evaluator a real signal on the modern-Chinese-bridges gap rather than masking it with iconic substitutions. The Humber / Great Belt / Sydney Harbour / New River Gorge alternatives are documented in proposed_supplements as future-cycle substitution candidates if benchmark design priorities shift toward LLM-knowability over source-faithfulness.
3) Bridge name normalization: Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved.
- '1915 Çanakkale Bridge': date prefix kept because 'Çanakkale Bridge' alone is ambiguous.
- 'Sutong Yangtze River Bridge', 'Yangsigang Yangtze River Bridge', 'Changtai Yangtze River Bridge': 'Yangtze River' qualifier kept because there are multiple bridges of the same primary name across other Chinese rivers.
- 'Akashi Kaikyō Bridge': Japanese macron ō (U+014D) preserved per Wikipedia article title; ASCII fallback 'Akashi Kaikyo Bridge' is the common-knowledge form but Wikipedia uses the macron.
- 'Tian'e Longtan Bridge': ASCII apostrophe (U+0027) preserved per Wikipedia URL form (Tian%27e). The pinyin form is 'Tiān'é' but Wikipedia article uses the simplified-apostrophe form.
- 'Forth Bridge' (cantilever, 1890): the railway bridge — not the suspension Forth Road Bridge (1964) which is a sibling structure across the Forth estuary.
4) Type values: 5 categorical values (Arch, Cable-stayed, Cantilever, Continuous truss, Suspension). Match the per-type Wikipedia master list categorization. The hyphenation in 'Cable-stayed' uses Wikipedia common-form (hyphenated compound). 'Continuous truss' uses two-word form per Wikipedia article title. No other structural types are staged in the universe (e.g., beam/girder bridges have shorter main spans and are not foregrounded in 'longest bridge' rankings).
5) Main Span (m) values: integer metres per the per-bridge Wikipedia article infobox + master-list main-span column for 16 of 17 staged bridges. Two-decimal precision is NOT used because the master lists report integer metres for all 17 staged bridges. For bridges where the master + per-bridge sources concur, the staged value matches both. For Pingnan Third Bridge (1 exception of 17), per-bridge article infobox + lead concur at 575 m while the master arch table reports 560 m without supporting per-bridge sourcing — staged value 575 m follows the cycle-2 refined canonical-source rule (per-bridge article wins for Main Span value when the per-bridge article is more detailed than the master table and infobox + lead concur). The Forth Bridge two-equal-main-spans case (each 521 m) is staged with the single-value report (521 m) matching both sources.
6) Country values: 7 distinct countries (China, Japan, United States, United Kingdom, Canada, Russia, Turkey). Stonecutters Bridge (Hong Kong) was staged in cycle-1 with Country = 'China' per master-list grouping but was displaced in cycle-2 by Husutong Yangtze River Bridge (mainland Jiangsu, China); the Hong Kong sub-national framing question is now moot for the post-cycle-2 staged universe (all 9 staged China rows are mainland China). The country-grouping rule (master-list grouping wins over sub-national framing) survives cycle-2 as a policy for future-cycle additions.
7) Year of Completion: numeric integer per per-bridge Wikipedia article. For staged bridges with multi-year construction phases (Forth Bridge built 1882-1890; Quebec Bridge built 1903-1917 after collapses; 1915 Çanakkale Bridge began construction 2017, opened 2022), the staged year is the calendar year of opening to traffic. Per-bridge articles use 'opened' / 'completed' / 'opened to traffic' framing — staged value follows the article-lead year.
8) Sort order: Type ASC primary (alphabetical: Arch, Cable-stayed, Cantilever, Continuous truss, Suspension), Main Span (m) DESC secondary (longest-first within each partition). For ties within a partition (Chaotianmen 552 m, Lupu 550 m — close but distinct), longest-first orders correctly. For exact ties (none in staged data), Bridge ASC alphabetical would tiebreak.
9) operation_type 'filter' chosen — top-K-per-type is structurally a filter operation (filter by type-rank within each partition; SQL ROW_NUMBER OVER (PARTITION BY type ORDER BY span DESC) <= K is filter-shape). 'aggregation' was considered (GROUP BY type with MAX span) but rejected because the universe includes all top-4 entries per type, not just the type-max — that's a row-level filter, not an aggregate.
10) claim_type 'source_defined' — universe is curator-bounded per the 4+1 partition rule (not strict top-K-uniform-K across all 5 types). The asymmetric partition is explicitly documented in temporal_note + curation.json::collection_summary + decision_log Decision 1. An `exhaustive` claim would require either top-4 across ALL 5 types (20 rows) or top-1 across ALL 5 types (5 rows) — both rejected at Stage-1 in favor of the 4+1 mixed partition.
normalization_decisions: Bridge (PK) values use Wikipedia common-form names with full disambiguator preserved per article title. Special-character handling: 'Akashi Kaikyō Bridge' uses Japanese macron ō (U+014D) per Wikipedia title; '1915 Çanakkale Bridge' uses Turkish cedilla Ç (U+00C7); 'Tian'e Longtan Bridge' uses ASCII apostrophe (U+0027) per Wikipedia URL form. Disambiguator preservation: '1915 Çanakkale Bridge' keeps the date prefix; Yangtze-river bridges keep 'Yangtze River' qualifier; 'Forth Bridge' is the 1890 cantilever railway bridge (not the 1964 Forth Road suspension bridge). Type is a single categorical value from a 5-value vocabulary (Arch / Cable-stayed / Cantilever / Continuous truss / Suspension); all 5 values appear in staged data. 'Cable-stayed' uses hyphenated form per Wikipedia common-form; 'Continuous truss' uses two-word form per Wikipedia common-form. Main Span (m) is numeric integer metres per per-bridge Wikipedia article infobox + master-list main-span column for 16 of 17 staged bridges; no decimal precision because all 17 staged values are integer metres. Pingnan Third Bridge (1 exception) uses 575 m per the per-bridge infobox + lead, deviating from the master arch table 560 m per the cycle-2 refined canonical-source rule. Country is a single categorical value (7 distinct values across staged rows). All 9 staged China rows are mainland China after cycle-2 (Stonecutters Bridge / Hong Kong was cycle-1 staged and cycle-2 displaced by Husutong Yangtze River Bridge / Jiangsu mainland); the master-list-grouping-over-sub-national rule survives cycle-2 as policy for future-cycle additions. Year of Completion is numeric integer per per-bridge Wikipedia article-lead 'opened' / 'completed' / 'opened to traffic' year (calendar year of opening to traffic for road bridges and for multi-year-construction bridges where the calendar year of opening is the canonical 'completion'). Sort: Type ASC primary (alphabetical), Main Span (m) DESC secondary.
open_questions: 1) The 4+1 partition asymmetry (top-4 for four primary types, top-1 for Continuous truss) is a curator-decision documented as `source_defined` claim type. Cycle-1 audit (no flag) and cycle-2 audit (no flag) accepted the asymmetry as adequately disclosed. A future audit cycle could still challenge this by proposing (a) strict top-4 across all 5 types (20 rows; would add 3 more continuous-truss entries below the visible engineering threshold), or (b) strict top-1 across all 5 types (5 rows). 2) Source-faithfulness vs LLM-knowability tradeoff: the staged universe includes obscure modern Chinese mega-bridges (Yangsigang, Nanjing Xianxin, Tian'e Longtan, Pingnan Third, Changtai Yangtze, Husutong) that the LLM may not know parametrically. The alternative — substituting iconic bridges (Humber, Great Belt East, Sydney Harbour, New River Gorge) into the Suspension and Arch partitions — was considered and rejected at Stage-1 in favor of strict source-faithfulness. An audit cycle could revisit this decision if benchmark design priorities shift toward LLM-knowability over source-faithfulness; the substituted alternatives are documented in proposed_supplements. 3) Pingnan Third Bridge main span discrepancy (575 m per-bridge article vs 560 m master arch table): cycle-2 audit HYGIENE H2 resolved by adopting 575 m per the cycle-2 refined canonical-source rule (per-bridge article wins for Main Span value when the per-bridge article is more detailed and infobox + lead concur). An LLM answering 560 m would be responding to the master-list cell value rather than the more-detailed per-bridge article. 4) Top-K ranking temporal-churn: cycle-2 caught two recent master-list displacements (Xihoumen → Nanjing Xianxin; Stonecutters → Husutong) and one year update (Changtai 2024 → 2025). The Cable-stayed top-4 and Suspension top-4 are particularly volatile — the universe rule (top-4 per primary type) is robust but specific rows may shift within 5-10 years as additional Chinese mega-bridges complete. A future audit cycle should re-check the top-K against the current master lists. 5) Forth Bridge (cantilever, 1890) vs Forth Road Bridge (suspension, 1964): the staged 'Forth Bridge' is the 1890 cantilever railway bridge; the 1964 Forth Road suspension bridge is a sibling structure but is NOT staged because at 1006 m main span it falls outside the Suspension top-4 (which the four staged suspension bridges occupy at 1700+ m post-cycle-2). An LLM might confuse the two — staged value is the cantilever-type Forth Bridge per master cantilever list. 6) Sydney Harbour Bridge (arch, 503 m, 1932, Australia): one of the most iconic arch bridges in the world but sits at #5-6 in the modern Arch top-N master ranking; NOT staged under the strict top-4 rule. An LLM answering with Sydney Harbour for the Arch type would be applying iconicity-judgment rather than source-faithful top-K. 7) Akashi Kaikyō macron normalization: staged with U+014D macron ō per Wikipedia article title. An LLM responding with 'Akashi Kaikyo' (ASCII fallback) is responding to the common-knowledge typographic simplification — both should be accepted under reasonable normalization. 8) Type field 'Cable-stayed' hyphenation: staged with hyphen per Wikipedia common-form. An LLM responding with 'Cable stayed' (no hyphen) or 'Cablestayed' (one word) is responding to alternative typographic conventions — the hyphenated form is the canonical Wikipedia rendering. 9) Quebec Bridge year 1917: the bridge completion was preceded by two famous collapses (1907, 1916); the staged year follows the per-bridge article's 'completed 1917' framing. An LLM answering 1916 (year of the second collapse) or 1919 (year of public opening) would be off by 1-2 years per alternative milestone framings. 10) Year of Completion for 1915 Çanakkale Bridge: '1915' is the date in the bridge's name (commemorating the 1915 Battle of Gallipoli), but the bridge was opened to traffic in 2022. An LLM answering 1915 (from the bridge name) is responding to the commemorative-name year rather than the opening-year — staged value is 2022 per per-bridge article lead.
proposed_supplements:
The 17-row staged universe is a curator-bounded subset of the world's longest bridges per the five per-type Wikipedia master lists. Two curator-decided scope choices and three substitution alternatives are documented:

(1) Partition-rule choice (4+1 vs strict top-K-uniform-K): the staged 4+1 asymmetric partition (top-4 for the four primary load-bearing types Suspension/Cable-stayed/Arch/Cantilever, plus top-1 for Continuous truss) is a curator-decision balance between universe-coverage and source-engineering-floor coherence. Strict alternatives:
- Strict top-4 across all 5 types (20 rows): would add Astoria-Megler (376 m, USA, 1966), Francis Scott Key Bridge (366 m, USA, 1977, collapsed 2024), and one more continuous truss bridge below ~360 m. Rejected because the additional continuous truss entries fall below the visible-engineering-threshold the other four types occupy at their 4th-place entries.
- Strict top-1 across all 5 types (5 rows): would lose 12 of the staged 17 rows. Rejected because 5-row universe is too small for meaningful top-K calibration.
- Strict top-3 across all 5 types (15 rows): would lose the four current 4th-place entries — Yangsigang (Suspension), Sutong (Cable-stayed), Lupu (Arch), Commodore Barry (Cantilever) — and add 2 continuous truss entries to bring Continuous truss to top-3 (so net 17 - 4 + 2 = 15 rows). Plausible alternative; rejected in favor of the 4+1 partition because 4-per-type is the more standard top-K depth in engineering rankings.

(2) Source-faithfulness vs LLM-knowability substitution alternatives: the staged universe includes obscure modern Chinese mega-bridges that the LLM may not know parametrically. Three substitution sets are documented as future-cycle alternatives if benchmark design priorities shift:
- Suspension partition substitutes: replace Nanjing Xianxin (1760 m, 2025) + Yangsigang (1700 m, 2019) with Humber Bridge (1410 m, UK, 1981) + Great Belt East Bridge (1624 m, Denmark, 1998). The Humber-substituted set sacrifices source-faithful top-4 for LLM-knowability of iconic Western/Northern-European suspension bridges. (Cycle-1 staged Xihoumen in this slot but cycle-2 displaced Xihoumen with Nanjing Xianxin per current master list ranking.)
- Arch partition substitutes: replace Tian'e Longtan (600 m, 2024) + Pingnan Third (575 m, 2020) with Sydney Harbour Bridge (503 m, Australia, 1932) + New River Gorge Bridge (518 m, USA, 1977). The substituted set replaces #1-#2 modern Chinese arches with iconic Western/Australian arches.
